recipes.name: Malaysian-Style Watermelon Salad
ingredients_raw: 2 (3 inch) pieces fresh ginger root, peeled and lightly crushed
2 teaspoons crushed red pepper flakes, or to taste
4 cups watermelon rind, white part only, cut into 1/2-inch cubes
0.5 cup peeled and chopped fresh ginger root
1 bunch cilantro, stems and leaves separated
12 cups chilled seedless watermelon, peeled and cut into 1-inch cubes

steps.text: Boil 1 ½ cups vinegar in a medium saucepan. Add 4 tablespoons brown sugar, crushed ginger, shallots, red pepper flakes, and 1 teaspoon salt. Stir until sugar and salt dissolve; remove pickling liquid from heat.
Place watermelon rind in a large bowl; strain pickling liquid through a fine-mesh strainer over rind. Stir to combine; refrigerate at least 1 hour.
Cook bacon in a large skillet over medium-high heat, turning occasionally, until evenly brown, about 10 minutes; drain on a paper towel-lined plate. Chop or crumble bacon into pieces when cool.

Place 1/2 cup chopped ginger, garlic, lime juice, cilantro stems, remaining 1 cup vinegar, remaining 2 tablespoons brown sugar, and remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt in a blender. Blend on high speed, scraping down jar occasionally, until dressing is mostly smooth.

To assemble the salad: Place 1 cup fresh watermelon on a plate, drizzle with 2 tablespoons dressing, top with 2 tablespoons pickled rind, 1 to 2 tablespoons bacon, 1 tablespoon cilantro leaves, and 1/2 tablespoon green onion.

raw_recipe.headline: Malaysian-Style Watermelon Salad
raw_recipe.description: This zesty Malaysian watermelon salad recipe includes bacon, homemade pickled watermelon rind, cilantro, and green onions in a gingery lime dressing.

review.reviewBody: Completely addictive! We cut the pickle and dressing recipes in half, and used one "personal" watermelon to make 8 servings (use an entire pound of bacon, though -- the bacon really makes the dish!) Be forewarned: the first bite is a little disconcerting, but you'll find that you have to take another... and another...

I followed the recipe without any changes other than leaving the bacon on the side for people to add as wanted - we have a few vegetarians in our extended family. Everyone loved it from the 2 year old to the 80 year old! My 3 teenagers in particular are asking to make it again. So glad I took a chance on this. I'm sure it will become a family staple during watermelon season.
I did slice the rind into thin strips instead of chunks. I also pickled extra rind and the kids are snacking on that. 
Thank you for the delicious recipe!
